dedupe_keys.name: green and blue space and heat related mortality burden in 1 085 subdistricts of zhejiang china ehp 2025

description: This study estimates how much urban green and blue space reduces deaths attributable to heat, using a case time-series of daily deaths from 2009 to 2020 in 1,085 subdistricts of Zhejiang province, China. Kejia Hu and colleagues from Zhejiang University, the Zhejiang Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Monash University published it in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2025. Coverage is the whole province at subdistrict level. Green and blue space exposure was measured from Baidu maps, OpenStreetMap and street view images. Scenarios show that 10, 20 and 30% more green space would avoid 1.6, 3.2 and 4.8% of the heat mortality burden, while the same increases in blue space would avoid 5.4, 10.8 and 16.2%. Format and access: an open access article on the journal site and PubMed Central, with a supplementary archive of code and data. Licence: EHP is free to read; the exact licence and the extent of shared data were not confirmed. Caveats: exposure proxies from maps and imagery, and effect sizes specific to one province. It gives inputs for climate adaptation planning of green and blue infrastructure against heat. Related catalogue records are the global urban heat island heatwave exposure data set and the Barcelona superblocks heat study.
